newsitem.title: USA: Brazil's Paging Network to return to US bond mart.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Paging Network to return to US bond mart.

text.p: After postponing its first-ever U.S. junk bond offering in early April due to poor market conditions, Paging Network do Brasil will once again attempt to tap the U.S. high-yield market in the next several weeks, according to market sources.
The company is planning to sell $125 million in junk bonds in the U.S. to finance the buildout of its startup paging and messaging services network, they said.
The 144a private placement will consist of $125 million in eight-year senior notes, they added.
Part of the proceeds will be set aside to pay investors a cash coupon for the first three years of the deal, the sources said.
They said Merrill Lynch & Co, the lead undewriter, will launch a roadshow for the offering next week.
Paging Network plans to begin offering paging services in greater Rio de Janeiro in 1998. The company began offering paging services in greater Sao Paulo in January of 1997.
Paging Network do Brasil is a private company, owned by Warburg Pincus Ventures LP, TVA Sistema de Televisao SA, the pay-TV subsidiary of Abril Group, and several investment funds.
Dallas-based paging company, Paging Network Inc, is the company's operating partner.
